ai.description: *Laudakia dayana* reaches 12 cm in snout-vent length. It features a grey-brown body with dark, irregular blotches and a distinctive row of enlarged, keeled scales along the flanks.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Laudakia dayana* is best distinguished from other Indian agamas by the presence of a distinct, enlarged, dark-edged patch on the throat, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Haridwar Agama inhabits rocky outcrops and boulder-strewn areas within dry deciduous forests and scrublands, typically at elevations ranging from 250 to 500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Haridwar Agama is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on rocky outcrops or brick walls to regulate its body temperature before actively foraging for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Laudakia dayana* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, generally between April and June.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Laudakia dayana* is endemic to the lower Himalayas of Uttarakhand, India, specifically inhabiting rocky terrain near Haridwar at elevations below 500 meters.
